SYNTHETIC INSURANCE COVERAGE POLICY DOCUMENT
This document contains synthetic test data only and is not a real insurance policy.

SECTION 1: TYPE 2 DIABETES MANAGEMENT COVERAGE
Coverage is available for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus management when the patient has a confirmed
diagnosis with ICD-10 code E11.x documented by a licensed physician. A current HbA1c value must
be present in the clinical record. Patients with HbA1c of 7.0 percent or higher qualify for
ongoing diabetes management coverage under this policy.

SECTION 2: HYPERTENSION AND BLOOD PRESSURE CRITERIA
Coverage for hypertension management requires documented blood pressure measurements in the
clinical record. For standard coverage tier, the patient's systolic blood pressure must be
below 160 mmHg at the time of evaluation. Patients presenting with systolic blood pressure
at or above 160 mmHg require additional clinical documentation and may be subject to
enhanced review before a coverage determination is issued.

SECTION 3: PRIOR AUTHORIZATION REQUIREMENTS
Certain medications require prior authorization before coverage is approved. Metformin
(biguanide class antidiabetic) requires a completed prior authorization request. The prior
authorization must include the treating physician's attestation, current HbA1c values, and
documentation that first-line dietary and lifestyle interventions have been attempted.
Dispensing without prior authorization will result in claim denial.

SECTION 4: ESCALATION AND HUMAN REVIEW CRITERIA
Cases that do not clearly satisfy all applicable coverage criteria must be escalated to the
medical review board for human review. Escalation is required when clinical documentation
is incomplete, ICD-10 codes are absent or ambiguous, key vital sign data is missing, or
when the clinical picture is inconsistent with the requested coverage category. Coverage
determinations cannot be issued automatically for escalated cases.

SECTION 5: DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
All coverage requests must include: (a) a signed clinical note from the treating provider,
(b) relevant diagnostic codes in ICD-10 format, (c) current medication list with dosages,
and (d) recent vital signs including blood pressure. Incomplete submissions will be returned
for additional documentation before a determination can be made.
